dossier.title: US Spot Bitcoin ETP Approval (January 2024)
dossier.claim: The U.S. SEC approved the listing and trading of multiple spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products on January 10, 2024.
dossier.market_question: Did the U.S. SEC approve spot Bitcoin ETPs on January 10, 2024?
dossier.resolution_criteria: Resolve SUPPORTED only if official SEC approval orders or Chair statement confirm approval dated 2024-01-10.

consensus.disagreement_summary: Corroborator and skeptic agreed on SUPPORTED (confidence gap 0.04).

passes.rationale: Primary SEC sources confirm the claim: Chair Gensler's January 10, 2024 statement says the Commission approved listing and trading of multiple spot bitcoin ETP shares that day, and SEC Release No. 34-99306 is the order granting accelerated approval of proposed rule changes to list and trade Bitcoin-based commodity-based trust shares dated January 10, 2024.

citations.excerpt: Today, the Commission approved the listing and trading of a number of spot bitcoin exchange-traded product (ETP) shares on January 10, 2024.

passes.rationale: Skeptic review found no material contradiction of the claim. The Chair statement dated 2024-01-10 says the Commission approved listing and trading of a number of spot bitcoin ETP shares that day, and SEC Release No. 34-99306 is an official order granting accelerated approval of proposed rule changes to list and trade Bitcoin-based ETP shares, also dated January 10, 2024. Public-evidence search returned those two official records as the only on-point matches. Residual caveats (Chair-statement URL slug 011023; source_id federal-register-34-99306 resolving to an SEC PDF rather than federalregister.gov) do not change the dated approval. Resolution criteria requiring official SEC approval orders or a Chair statement dated 2024-01-10 are therefore met.

dx_findings.title: Internal Structured Classifier Turns (FreshnessContract / FinalizationStatus / ClosureJudgment)
dx_findings.observation: openminion==0.1.21 emits out-of-band tool_choice='submit_output' requests with JSON schema titles `FreshnessContract`, `FinalizationStatus`, and `ClosureJudgment`. In closure evaluation, `[JUDGE CONTEXT]` supplies `action_summary:` while `final_close_message()` prefers `ClosureJudgment.final_answer` over `action_result.summary`, so gateways/stubs handling `ClosureJudgment` must preserve `action_summary` / `closure_action_summary` or risk overwriting structured JSON answers.

dx_findings.title: Explicit thread_id Required for Multi-Turn Agent.run(session_id=...) Continuity
dx_findings.observation: Calling `Agent.run(..., session_id=session_a)` returns an allocated `thread_id` (`metadata['thread_id']`); without passing `thread_id=turn1.thread_id` on subsequent calls, `openminion==0.1.21` starts a fresh conversation thread even with matching `session_id`. Forwarding both `session_id` and `thread_id` retains transcript history while separate `session_id` values remain isolated.

dx_findings.title: AnthropicProvider (/v1/messages + x-api-key) vs OpenAI-Compatible & Cortensor Adapters
dx_findings.observation: `AnthropicProvider` sends POST `{base_url}/messages` with `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version` headers (`accept: text/event-stream` for streaming), whereas `OpenAIProvider` and `CortensorProvider` use Bearer auth (`Authorization: Bearer ...`) against `/chat/completions` or `/api/v2/completions`.

dx_findings.title: Inline Boolean approval_callback vs Async RuntimeTurnHandle.resolve_approval()
dx_findings.observation: `Agent.run(..., approval_callback=...)` bridges a synchronous/awaitable boolean guard onto the brain worker thread (observed 2 callback invocations across allow & deny gates on `@tool(dangerous=True, min_scope='WRITE_SAFE')`). In contrast, `APIRuntime.submit_turn()` sets `approval_transport='turn_stream'` and requires stream consumers to resolve `approval` chunks via `handle.resolve_approval(approval_id=..., decision='allow_once'|'deny')` with bounded wait timeouts.

dx_findings.title: Windows SQLite Worktree Isolation & http_connection_reuse_enabled=False
dx_findings.observation: Passing explicit `home_root` and `data_root` isolates `.openminion/agents.json` and SQLite/Alembic state per worktree on Windows. Disabling `http_connection_reuse_enabled=False` avoids persistent `httpx.Client` socket reuse (`http_client_for_config()` returns `None` and falls back to `urllib.request.urlopen`), preventing stale keep-alive errors across ephemeral or loopback endpoints.

dx_findings.title: Layered Retry Multiplication, SSE Usage Gating & TurnTelemetry vs stats
dx_findings.observation: On HTTP 500 with `provider_retry_max_attempts=2`, observed 6 HTTP attempts because `LLMCTLBridgeProvider` adds inner transport retries (`max_retries=2`) inside `BrainRunner`'s outer retry loop. `submit_turn()` captured 12 TurnChunk(s) with `TurnTelemetry(duration_ms=6281, tokens_in=0, tokens_out=0)` vs `TurnResponse.stats(input_tokens=11841, output_tokens=430)`: `daemon.py` reads `metadata.get('usage_prompt_tokens')`, whereas the runtime populates `total_input_tokens_used` and `stats`. Additionally, `OpenAIProvider.stream()` skips SSE `usage` chunks unless `provider_identity={'service_vendor': 'openai'}` enables `preserve_response_facts`.

dx_findings.title: 90s Turn-Timeout Default, Handoff Forwarding Gap & Live Paraphrasing
dx_findings.observation: `Agent.run(..., timeout_seconds=None)` defaults internal turn timeout to `90.0s` regardless of `OpenMinionConfig` provider HTTP timeouts unless `timeout_seconds` is explicitly forwarded to BOTH `Agent.run(timeout_seconds=...)` and `subagent(timeout_seconds=...)`. Multi-tool reasoning turns routinely span multiple round-trips (`classifier + tool + finalization`). Furthermore, in `openminion/api/handoff.py:169`, `build_delegate_tool()` calls `handoff.target.run(message)` without forwarding caller `timeout_seconds` or `approval_callback`, leaving peer handoff targets on the `90.0s` default turn timeout and requiring `PolicyGrantInput` on the target runtime for `allow_once` gating. Additionally, live LLMs execute `Handoff` (`transfer_to_specialist`) cleanly and paraphrase the specialist confirmation in coordinator prose rather than echoing synthetic marker tokens verbatim.

dx_findings.title: Structured Output Envelope Collision (`respond(answer, freshness)` + `agent_id:` Prefix)
dx_findings.observation: In `openminion==0.1.21`, `runtime.run_turn()` formats `body` with an `f'{agent_id}: '` prefix, causing `Agent._coerce_output()`'s initial `output_type.model_validate_json(text)` to fail and rely on `_extract_json_object(text)`. Meanwhile, `BrainRunner`'s entry prompt instructs direct replies using `respond(answer=..., freshness=...)`; some live models occasionally emit that outer envelope as assistant text (`agent: {"answer": "{...}", "freshness": {...}}`), causing `_extract_json_object()` to extract the outer `freshness` wrapper instead of the inner JSON payload and raise `AgentOutputValidationError`. Explicitly commanding single-line RFC-8259 double-quoted JSON and avoiding unquoted pseudo-schemas improves compliance.

dx_findings.title: Shared Session & Parallel Tool-Call `task_update` Collision (`resolve_entry_task_update`)
dx_findings.observation: In `openminion/modules/brain/loop/context/task_context.py:153-191`, `resolve_entry_task_update()` raises `ValueError` (`'Missing task_update'` or `'Exactly one task_update is allowed per entry response'`), turning the reply into the fallback clarification `'I could not safely update the task conditions...'` whenever an active session receives sequential `subagent()` calls sharing the same raw `session_id` or when a model batches multiple tool calls carrying duplicate `task_update` sidecars. Giving each subagent pass an isolated runtime `session_id` while persisting cross-turn citations in explicit `MemoryBundle` state avoids the crash.
